results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database (VFB). According to VFB, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch that have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds various records related to the mushroom body, including neurons with some part in the mushroom body, parts of the mushroom body, and images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body, with counts of [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body"), [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body"), and [22137](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in mushroom body") records, respectively.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The Virtual Fly Brain (VFB) database indicates that there are multiple types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain. VFB records show several subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), including [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, VFB data suggests that Kenyon cells can be further categorized into types such as alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, with subtypes including core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes. VFB has annotated [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell. For more information, you can explore the available data on Kenyon cell, such as images ([31468](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of Kenyon cell") records), scRNAseq data ([79](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for Kenyon cell") records), transgene expression ([91](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in Kenyon cell") records), downstream connectivity classes ([866](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell") records), and upstream connectivity classes ([1006](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell") records).

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response:
The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") is connected to various brain regions through tracts and nerves. According to VFB, the antennal lobe is connected to the mushroom body and lateral horn. VFB records show that any antennal lobe projection neuron that sends synaptic output to the mushroom body, specifically the mushroom body calyx, and/or the lateral horn. 

VFB holds data on tracts and nerves innervating the antennal lobe, with [32](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating antennal lobe") records. It also holds data on neurons with some part in the antennal lobe, including those with synaptic terminals, presynaptic terminals, and postsynaptic terminals, with [676](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe"), [673](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in antennal lobe"), [266](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in antennal lobe"), and [512](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in antennal lobe") records respectively. 

To explore the connections of the antennal lobe further, you can examine the available images of the antennal lobe, or investigate the neurons with some part in the antennal lobe, and the parts and subclasses of the antennal lobe. VFB has annotated a substantial amount of data related to the antennal lobe, which can be used to understand its connectivity.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
VFB has annotated [9413](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047887,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central brain") neuron types with some part in the [adult central brain](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047887 "Open adult central brain in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, the connectome data indicates more than 125,000 neurons. However, it's essential to note that the "neurons with some part here" figure represents the number of neuron types annotated in VFB, not the biological total. For an accurate biological total, one would need to consult published literature, but no such reference is provided in the available evidence.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.question: I want to image neurons in the lateral horn. What split-GAL4 driver lines are available that target lateral horn neuron types?

VFB holds 176 records of transgene expression in the lateral horn, including examples such as [P{DAT-B-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{ple-p65.AD.TH-F} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0129936FBtp0129969 "Open P{DAT-B-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{ple-p65.AD.TH-F} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain") and [P{DAT-B-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{ple-p65.AD.TH-D} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0129936FBtp0129968 "Open P{DAT-B-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{ple-p65.AD.TH-D} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The LPLC2 visual neuron type is described as a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron. According to the VFB database, its cell body lies in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind, as noted by Wu et al., 2016. The LPLC2 visual neuron type has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer. These dendritic arbors extend outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, as described by Klapoetke et al., 2017. VFB does not currently hold specific data on the connections of the LPLC2 visual neuron type beyond its dendritic structure in the lobula plate layers. The function of the LPLC2 visual neuron type is related to motion detection, given the orientation of its dendritic arbors. VFB holds information on the LPLC2 visual neuron type, including its classification as a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron. For more detailed information on its connectivity and function, further queries can be made to explore available data in VFB.

results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") in adult Drosophila has approximately 50 glomeruli, whereas in larval Drosophila it has around 22 glomeruli, indicating that the [adult antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007401 "Open adult antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") is more elaborated than the larval antennal lobe, as recorded in VFB. VFB holds various data related to the antennal lobe, including images, neurons with different types of terminals, parts, subclasses, and tracts/nerves innervating it. For example, VFB has annotated [676](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe") neurons with some part in antennal lobe and [100](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of antennal lobe") parts of antennal lobe. To further compare the organisation of the antennal lobe between adult and larval Drosophila, you can explore the available images of antennal lobe, neurons with synaptic terminals in antennal lobe, or lineage clones found in antennal lobe.

results.title: Publications for a circuit
results.question: What publications describe the PPL1 dopaminergic neurons and their role in aversive memory?
results.response: Publications by Mao and Davis (2009) and Claridge-Chang et al. (2009) describe the dopaminergic PPL1 neurons and their role in aversive memory. The connectome data indicates that dopaminergic PPL1 neurons are involved in aversive memory, as Mao and Davis (2009) identify 8 protocerebral clusters coincidentally positive for TH-GAL4 activity and tyrosine hydroxylase immunoreactivity, implying these cells are dopaminergic. VFB holds [385](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100219,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of PPL1") images of dopaminergic PPL1 neurons, and has annotated [18](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100219,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of PPL1") subclasses of dopaminergic PPL1 neurons, as well as transgene expression in dopaminergic PPL1 neurons ([89](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100219,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in PPL1") records), downstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic PPL1 neurons ([849](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100219,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for PPL1") records), and upstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic PPL1 neurons ([1279](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00100219,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for PPL1") records).

results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?
results.response:
The connectome data indicates that there are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons. VFB records show 22 reciprocal class-level pairs between these two neuron types. The direction from [dopaminergic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005131 "Open dopaminergic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") to [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") has a partner count of 77, while the direction from mushroom body output neuron to dopaminergic neuron has a partner count of 94. The target-to-source weight is 7620 and the source-to-target weight is 2697. 

VFB holds a substantial amount of data on both mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons, including downstream and upstream connectivity classes, which may provide further insight into their connections. For mushroom body output neurons, VFB has annotated [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream connectivity classes and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes. For dopaminergic neurons, VFB has annotated [8845](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") downstream connectivity classes and [7914](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") upstream connectivity classes. 

To identify the pairs with the strongest mutual connectivity, further analysis of the top partners and their corresponding weights would be necessary. VFB does not currently hold specific data on the strongest mutual connections between individual pairs of mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response:
The pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn involves intermediate neuron types. According to VFB, a high-level pathway is: [olfactory receptor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005926 "Open olfactory receptor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> lateral horn. This indicates that antennal lobe projection neurons receive olfactory input in the antennal lobe and send axons to higher brain centers, including the lateral horn. 

VFB holds data on neurons with some part in [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain") ([1661](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult lateral horn") records) and neurons with synaptic terminals in adult lateral horn ([1658](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult lateral horn") records), which may be relevant for understanding the connections within this pathway. Additionally, VFB has annotated downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron ([575](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") records) and upstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron ([379](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") records), which could provide further insight into the specific connections between olfactory receptor neurons and other neuron types, including antennal lobe projection neurons. 

To further explore this pathway, you can query VFB for specific neuron types and their connections, such as neurons postsynaptic to olfactory receptor neurons or presynaptic to neurons in the lateral horn.

results.title: Cell type taxonomy depth
results.question: How many distinct neuron types are currently classified within the adult Drosophila visual system, and how are they organised hierarchically?
results.response:

results.question: I want to study the neural circuit underlying CO2 avoidance in Drosophila. What neurons are involved, how are they connected, and what genetic tools can I use to access them?
results.response:
To study the neural circuit underlying CO2 avoidance in Drosophila, it's essential to identify the neurons involved, their connections, and the genetic tools available to access them. However, VFB does not currently hold specific data on the neural circuit underlying CO2 avoidance in Drosophila. 

The connectome data indicates that certain neurons, such as those expressing the Gr21a and Gr63a receptors, are involved in CO2 detection (as reported by Suh et al., 2004, and others). VFB holds records of these receptors and their expression in certain neurons, but it does not currently hold comprehensive data on the specific neural circuit underlying CO2 avoidance.

Regarding connectivity, VFB records show connections between certain neurons in the antennal lobe and higher-order olfactory centers, but it does not currently hold detailed data on the connectivity of neurons specifically involved in CO2 avoidance.

For accessing these neurons, genetic tools such as GAL4 drivers and Split-GAL4 systems can be used. VFB has annotated several GAL4 drivers that target specific neurons in the Drosophila brain, but it does not currently hold data on which drivers specifically target CO2-avoidance neurons.

To further investigate the neural circuit underlying CO2 avoidance, you can explore VFB's data on Drosophila neurons, their receptors, and genetic tools. The giant fiber neuron is associated with certain GAL4 drivers, which have specific expression patterns. VFB has annotated data on the expression patterns of these drivers, which can be used to study the giant fiber neuron.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response:
Based on connectivity data, several neuron types might mediate a connection between the [visual system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047735 "Open visual system in Virtual Fly Brain") and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB records show that neurons such as [ML-VPN2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052139 "Open ML-VPN2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052141 "Open Mt-VPN1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052140 "Open Mt-VPN in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mti](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052142 "Open Mti in Virtual Fly Brain"), [T4ai neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052241 "Open T4ai neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") have some part in the visual system, and neurons like [CB2311](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20005873 "Open CB2311 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [CB2443](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20005995 "Open CB2443 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [CB3379](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20006842 "Open CB3379 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [MB-C2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100228 "Open MB-C2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [MB-M1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100229 "Open MB-M1 in Virtual Fly Brain") have some part in the mushroom body. Additionally, the connectome data indicates that adult visual projection neurons, which have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, could also facilitate this connection, as reported by Vogt et al., 2016, and Yagi et al., 2016. 

VFB holds a substantial amount of data on neurons related to both the visual system and the mushroom body, including [1046](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047735,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in visual system") neurons with some part in the visual system and [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body. The data also includes information on neurons with synaptic terminals, presynaptic terminals, and postsynaptic terminals in both the visual system and the mushroom body. 

Given this connectivity data, it is possible that visual information could reach the memory circuit via these neuron types, suggesting a potential pathway for visual information to influence memory processes in the mushroom body. However, the specific details of this connectivity would depend on the exact neurons and their connections involved.
